title: Persimmon, Radicchio & Pomegranate Salad
description: “The vibrant colors and delicious flavor make this a showstopper for the holidays” says Ayesha Nurdjaja of the Shuka and Shukette restaurants in NYC. Persimmons make a colorful cool weather salad, combined with red radicchio leaves and glistening ruby-like pomegranate seeds. You need the small apple-size Fuyu persimmons, which are delicious eaten raw. (The pointy Hachiya persimmons need to ripen to softness and are usually cooked for cakes or puddings.) Make this throughout the fall and winter. If persimmons are unavailable use pears, Asian pears or crisp tart apples.
ingredients: 2 ounces blue or goat cheese, crumbled
½ cup hazelnuts, toasted and roughly chopped (optional)
directions: Whisk together olive oil, honey, molasses, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, and salt in a bowl until well-combined and emulsified. Adjust the ingredients to taste.

Cut the heads of radicchio in half lengthwise. Remove cores, and gently separate the leaves. Similarly, separate the endive leaves. Place in a large bowl. (You can tear or cut these up into bite-sized pieces if preferred.)
Cut the persimmon into bite-sized chunks or little wedges (optionally peeling). Drizzle with a little dressing and toss to combine.
Arrange the lettuces on a platter. Top with pomegranate arils, chives, cheese, and nuts (optional). Drizzle with a little more dressing.
